docs.title: Setting up the app from scratch
docs.desc: Setting up from scratch with screenshots from the app's own test: the RunPod keys (API, SSH, registry login, S3), Default Configuration, a network volume, a pod, and what each failure means.

docs.title: Quick Start - See ComfyUI Working
docs.desc: Three ways to see ComfyUI working in minutes: the RunPod dashboard, a local install, or a real RunPod pod. Comparison and recommended path.

docs.title: Setup Guide - On-Demand Pod
docs.desc: Deploying an on-demand RunPod pod: prerequisites, GPU choice, deployment steps, wiring the comfy CLI to it, cost tracking, pod management. Not done yet; status and the CANALV2 plan are in NEXT-STEPS.md.

docs.title: Local ComfyUI Setup
docs.desc: Running ComfyUI on your own machine instead of RunPod: options, hardware, speed comparison, model handling, switching between local and cloud. The current local install is apps/comfy-app.

docs.title: Workflows Guide
docs.desc: How workflows are organised in the comfy CLI project format: fragments, blueprints, composing, versioning, testing, best practices.

docs.title: ComfyUI MOE Architecture
docs.desc: The full picture of the pod orchestration stack: the three-layer design (Claude Code → MCP server → pool manager → RunPod), components, data flows, auth, deployment scenarios, scaling.

docs.title: ADR-001 · RunPod Deployment Strategy - Hybrid Serverless + On-Demand
docs.desc: Why a hybrid of on-demand pods (development now) and serverless endpoints (batch rendering later), with trade-offs and migration path.

docs.title: ADR-002 · Mixture of Experts (MOE) Agent Pool Infrastructure
docs.desc: The "mixture of experts" agent pool: a pool of RunPod pods shared by several users and agents, with implementation plan, costs, quotas, credentials and rollout.

docs.title: ADR-003 · Python + MCP vs. Terraform for POD Orchestration
docs.desc: Why pod orchestration is Python plus an MCP server rather than Terraform, alternatives considered, and when to revisit.

docs.title: ADR-006 · The ComfyUI image is built on CI next to a private registry; workflows ride on the volume
docs.desc: The ComfyUI image lives in a private GitLab registry and is built and pushed on GitLab CI next to it (the 3 GB torch layer never leaves the Mac); pods pull with a saved credential; workflows ride on the volume, seeded from the image only while empty; sshd in the image for the sync. Accepted 2026-10-20.

docs.title: ADR-007 · How local state and the pod's volume stay in line
docs.desc: How local state and the pod's volume stay in line: the per-folder contract (who writes where), the options from "add Pull to the script" through "Push and Pull in the app" to "a bucket as the hub", a recommendation, and the decision left open. Proposed 2026-10-20, no decision yet.

docs.title: ADR-009 · The Adapter Studio: chat builds a prompt, the prompt builds the adapter
docs.desc: The Adapter Studio: one IDE-style modal for Edit, New adapter and Write an adapter with Claude: code and prompt tabs, Code / Preview / Split icon buttons, the package as a tree with a file viewer, Claude's chat that builds an editable prompt which builds the adapter, built-ins editable by override, naming, documentation as a rule on generation, agentic validation on save, no autosave. Built 2026-10-24.

docs.title: ADR-010 · A screen always says which app it is in
docs.desc: A full-screen screen always carries the app's mark and name (and the no-spend badge) in its header. Accepted 2026-10-24.

docs.title: ADR-011 · What a sync carries, and what it does with what is already there
docs.desc: What a sync carries: which ComfyUI-Shared folders go and come back, skipping renders and the test bucket, what to do with files already on the pod, the skipped counter.

docs.title: ADR-012 · the app is released by version
docs.desc: The app is released by semantic version (patch unless Lucas names one), tagged vX.Y.Z, installers on the public downloads repo's Releases. Accepted 2026-10-27.

docs.title: ADR-014 · the documentation is a public site built from the README
docs.desc: The documentation is a public Pages site built from this section: the README is the navigation, client-job docs are left out by a list, the setup walkthrough's screenshots come from a test. Accepted 2026-10-27.

docs.title: ADR-013 · how the app is delivered
docs.desc: How the app is delivered: one Pages site, a button per platform (dmg, exe, Linux), versioned files with stable aliases, unsigned for now. Accepted 2026-10-27.

docs.title: Dockerfile Deviations from Official RunPod/ComfyUI
docs.desc: Review of the original placeholder image (community ashleykza/comfyui base) against RunPod's official one. That placeholder is retired; the current image is apps/comfy-app/Dockerfile, built on pytorch/pytorch with the same pins as the Mac.

docs.title: The two MCP endpoints
docs.desc: The two MCP endpoints tool by tool: the pod manager (pool, pods, volumes, configuration, sync, cost; named yes where it spends) and the ComfyUI bridge (a local agent inside the ComfyUI of a pod: workflows, nodes, queue, history, outputs; refuses locked shots), the client connectors (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, ChatGPT over HTTP) and the Connect › MCP tab.

docs.title: The ComfyUI API, as this repo uses it
docs.desc: The ComfyUI HTTP API as this repo uses it: health and readiness, the Workflows panel's userdata calls, queueing a graph, queue and history, the two graph formats, and which of our files call what.

docs.title: Infrastructure Setup
docs.desc: The infrastructure folder: the pod lifecycle CLI, pod config, where the Docker image and the API live, cost management, monitoring, troubleshooting.

docs.title: MCP Server: ComfyUI Agent Pool Control
docs.desc: The MCP server that exposes agent pool management to Claude Code: quick start, every tool, typical sessions, configuration, errors, budgeting.

docs.title: apps/comfy-app
docs.desc: The ComfyUI server project: what is upstream and what is ours (check.sh), running from a fresh clone, the Docker image, pointing the comfy CLI at it, targets and open approvals.

docs.title: RunPod dashboard (`apps/runpod-dashboard`)
docs.desc: The Vue dashboard for the pod manager: features, architecture, API integration, dev and production builds, the Electron desktop app.

docs.title: Frontend — components and styling
docs.desc: Component-by-component reference for the dashboard UI, styling conventions and the Electron packaging.

docs.title: Testing
docs.desc: The app's tests: the core suite (Vitest), the browser suite against a fake API (Playwright), the Electron suite in no-spend mode, the live RunPod proof, the MCP and CLI tests; what each covers and how to run them.
